question: After runtime's verified byte-preserving nginx HIT-cache substrate (oracle-free decompression 960/960 byte-identical across HIT/SWR/SIE/304 stages), does a controlled single-resource local perturbation (DOM attribute/text change, endpoint param/header change, Cache-Control/ETag mutation) require only localized repair — bounded tokens/browser/verification cost and contamination < threshold — versus full re-exploration, with repair cost amortized over retrieval frequency?
hypothesis: C-DELTA-REPAIR hypothesis: a single-resource local perturbation is repairable by a localized patch (re-target selector, rebind param slot, update header expectation, refresh cache key) without re-exploring the full task. Expected: (1) localized repair succeeds on >=80% of perturbation instances; (2) mean repair cost <50% of full cold re-exploration cost in tokens and <40% in browser interactions; (3) verification step detects incorrect repair (catches false accepts) with precision >=0.9; (4) contamination of unrelated mechanisms <10%; (5) amortized cost (repair + verification + n_reuses*retrieval) < full re-exploration cost when n_reuses >=5-10. Byte-preserving HIT-cache substrate guarantees cache correctness is orthogonal: decompressed body identity across HIT/SWR/SIE/304 is 960/960 before perturbations, so any post-perturbation divergence is attributable to the controlled local change, not decompression artefacts.
falsifier: C-DELTA-REPAIR is falsified (in this setting) if ANY primary locality condition fails: (F1) repair success rate <0.80 across all perturbation instances; (F2) mean repair token cost >=0.50 * mean full-re-exploration token cost OR mean browser interactions >=0.40 * full; (F3) contamination (fraction of unrelated mechanisms that become invalid or false-accept after patch) >=0.10; (F4) verification fails to discriminate correct vs incorrect repair (AUROC <0.75 or precision <0.80 at operating threshold); (F5) amortized repair not cheaper than full re-exploration at n_reuses=10. A global falsification requires failure across all three perturbation families; family-specific failure (e.g., DOM only) bounds the ceiling rather than falsifying the entire claim.

baselines.description: Full cold re-exploration: LLM agent (same model, same tools, same budget) solves the task from scratch with empty registry and no prior trajectory. Measures full task cost in tokens, browser interactions, latency, and verification calls. This is the cost delta-repair must amortize against.
baselines.expected: Succeeds on >=90% tasks but at full cost (baseline 100%). Repair must be <50% tokens and <40% browser steps.

baselines.description: Verbatim mechanism/route replay without repair: stored mechanism from pre-perturbation executed unchanged on post-perturbation target. Strong 0-token replay baseline from Frontier/Intel prior (TERX/BrowserBash class).
baselines.expected: Near 0% success post-perturbation (correctly fails). Demonstrates replay alone is insufficient and that repair adds value beyond trivial reuse. If replay succeeds, perturbation was non-breaking.

baselines.description: Semantic retrieval over prior trajectory memory (embedding search + nearest successful trajectory replay). Represents strong retrieval baseline that Graph must beat to justify repair mechanics over RAG.
baselines.expected: Partial success: retrieves correct trajectory family but fails on stale locator/header without local patch (expected 20-40% success). Repair should exceed retrieval by >=30pp success.

baselines.description: Oracle hand-authored minimal patch (single selector/param/header correction) applied by experimenter, executed and verified. Upper-bound ceiling for achievable localized repair.
baselines.expected: 100% success with 1 browser probe + 1 verification. Provides cost ceiling; measured repair should approach oracle (within 2x tokens/steps).

baselines.description: Runtime verified substrate invariant: oracle-free decompression (Content-Encoding handling without oracle) yields 960/960 byte-identical decompressed bodies across HIT, SWR (stale-while-revalidate), SIE (stale-if-error), and 304 Not Modified stages on unperturbed resources.
baselines.expected: 960/960 identical; recomputed SHA256(body) HIT==SWR==SIE==304. If this baseline drifts, measurement is invalid per C-MEAS-VALID.

positive_control.description: Two positive controls: (PC1) Unperturbed execution: mechanism resolved and verified on pre-perturbation endpoint with no patch succeeds and verify()=true, byte identity 1.0. (PC2) Known-break single-attribute perturbation with oracle patch: Flask+nginx testbed where target DOM id changes from #submit-123 to #submit-124 and oracle patch updates selector; repair succeeds within 2 browser probes and verification passes. Also endpoint param rename ?id= -> ?item= with oracle rebinding. Both must show repair success, byte identity after repair equals expected new resource, and cost < full re-exploration.
positive_control.expected: PC1 100% success, PC2 >=90% success with cost ratio <0.5 vs B-COLD. If either fails, instrumentation is broken, not the hypothesis.

null_control.description: Two null controls: (NC1) Zero perturbation (identical pre/post resource): proposed repair pipeline must produce zero patch (repair cost 0, contamination 0, verify no false patch) and byte identity 1.0 across all cache stages. (NC2) Distant unrelated perturbation (modify endpoint B while target is endpoint A): repair of A must be no-op, success on A unchanged, and contamination measurement on B-independent mechanisms remains 0. Both tested with permutation-shuffled repair decisions (random patch proposal) to verify false-accept detection.
null_control.expected: NC1 repair cost =0, NC2 contamination =0, both with false-accept rate 0%. Random-patch null shows verification precision thresholding works (AUROC ~0.5 for random).

measurement_validity: Substrate provenance: nginx reverse-proxy with HIT/SWR/SIE/304 caching (Cache-Control max-age, stale-while-revalidate, stale-if-error), Flask backend with PyJWT HS256 auth, decompression via oracle-free path (raw Content-Encoding handling, not oracle decompression), verified 960/960 byte-identical decompressed bodies pre-perturbation (SHA256(body) HIT==SWR==SIE==304). Runtime dependency: research/runtime nginx HIT-cache fixture or reproduced equivalent; record nginx.conf, Flask testbed_server.py commit, decompression code hash.

Perturbation isolation (single-resource): each instance mutates exactly one local resource — one DOM node attribute (id/class/data-testid) OR one text node OR one endpoint query param/header name OR one response header (Cache-Control max-age value, ETag value). No global config, no auth migration, no multi-resource drift. Perturbation manifest records file, line, old/new value, and blast radius =1 resource. Cross-condition contamination checked by re-reading unrelated resources.

Pre/post registry snapshot isolation: registry cloned before perturbation; repair operates on clone; contamination measured as delta on uninvolved mechanism set (N>=20 unrelated mechanisms). No leakage of perturbation description into repair prompt beyond post-state observation (no oracle label). Repair agent sees only pre-perturbation mechanism + post-perturbation page/response observation + verify() signal.

Cost measurement transparency: tokens = sum(prompt+completion) for repair LLM calls (record model id, temperature, max_tokens), browser interactions = count(Playwright actions: goto, click, fill, evaluate, network fetch), verification cost = count(verify() + registry lookup + HIT-cache fetch), wall-time measured. Full re-exploration cost measured with identical budget/metrics. Retrieval cost included in amortized calculation.

Verification validity: verify(mechanism_id, observed_state) checks postconditions (_matches) on actual response/DOM state, not on expected label. False accepts measured as verify()=true but observed_state functionally wrong (checked by independent oracle script using ground-truth selector/param). Directional correctness: post-state never leaks into pre-state features for verification threshold calibration (fit threshold on TRAIN perturbations only).

Adequacy: >=36 perturbation instances (3 families x 2 variants x 6 seeds/instances), >=20 unrelated mechanisms for contamination, >=10 reuse amortizations. Each family has independent success/cost reported; pooled only when family is homogeneous. If any family has n<12, mark as underpowered exploratory.

Determinism: fixed seeds for perturbation generation, nginx cache key generation, and LLM repair (where supported); all hashes use hashlib.sha256, never Python hash(); record commit, Python version, nginx version, Playwright version. Exclude flaky network/external sites — localhost nginx+Flask only.

Byte-identity recomputation: for each instance, store SHA256(decompressed_body) for HIT, SWR, SIE, 304 pre and post; post-perturbation HIT body for perturbed resource must differ from pre (mutation detected) while unperturbed resources remain 960/960-equivalent subset (or proportional). Oracle-free decompression code path preserved from runtime fixture.
decision_rule: All thresholds applied on frozen pre-registered data only. Compute per-instance metrics then aggregate. Gates: (C1) PC1 success=1.0 and PC2 repair success >=0.90; else MEASUREMENT_INVALID. (C2) NC1 cost=0 and NC2 contamination=0 and random-patch false-accept <=5%; else MEASUREMENT_INVALID (repair pipeline mis-calibrated). (C3) B-RUNTIME-BYTE-IDENTITY 960/960-equivalent pre-perturbation byte identity >=0.99 (allow 1% tooling jitter); else MEASUREMENT_INVALID. Primary gates (require ALL to CONFIRM localized repair): (C4) repair success rate >=0.80 pooled AND >=0.70 per family; (C5) mean repair tokens <0.50 * mean B-COLD tokens AND mean browser interactions <0.40 * B-COLD AND mean verification steps <=2; (C6) contamination <0.10 (fraction unrelated mechanisms invalidated or false-accept); (C7) verification AUROC >=0.75 and precision at operating threshold >=0.80; (C8) amortized cost at n_reuses=10 (repair + verification + 10*retrieval_cost) < B-COLD cost (tokens and browser). CONFIRMED if C1-C8 all PASS. FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING if any of C4-C8 fails while C1-C3 PASS (valid negative). MEASUREMENT_INVALID if any of C1-C3 fails or n<24 or substrate byte identity fails. MIXED if family-heterogeneous: >=1 family passes C4-C8 while another fails — report per-family ceilings. Effect sizes, CIs (95% Wilson for rates, bootstrap for cost ratios), and per-family breakdown required.
product_consequence_positive: If CONFIRMED, C-DELTA-REPAIR advances from HYPOTHESIS toward EXPERIMENTAL/VALIDATED for single-resource local perturbations on nginx HIT-cache localhost substrate. Justifies product architecture with localized repair boundaries: registry patch + verify loop rather than full task replay, with amortized cost advantage after 5-10 reuses. Next steps: expand perturbation radius (2-3 resources, cross-page), test on distributed Redis session store, and integrate repair into SpiderKernel.invalidate()+distill() pipeline with freshness guard. Promotion to Product Core NOT authorized — localhost nginx only, synthetic perturbations, single model.
product_consequence_negative: If FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING, single-resource locality fails even under minimal perturbations, closing the smallest repair hypothesis. Product must default to full re-exploration or fused RAG+re-exploration for any drift, and must budget repair as equivalent to cold cost. Delta-repair claim remains HYPOTHESIS at best, blocked for broader radius. Implications: (a) do not invest in single-selector rebinding until stronger isolation/representation is proven; (b) runtime HIT-cache substrate validated for measurement but not sufficient for repair; (c) Graph lane should pivot to C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY with matched families or C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE with abstention calibration, both of which do not assume cheap local patches. A valid negative here is high information — it prevents shipping a repair layer that would cause contamination/false accepts.
estimated_cost: Low-Medium: reuse runtime nginx+Flask fixture (0.5h setup), generate 36 perturbation instances (1h), run B-COLD (1h, LLM + Playwright), run repair+verify loop per instance (1h), run retrieval baseline (0.5h), compute byte identity + contamination (0.5h), analysis (0.5h). Total ~5 compute-hours, no external API beyond single LLM model; all localhost.
expected_information_gain: Very high: first ever measurement of C-DELTA-REPAIR (0/224 canonical experiments). Directly tests SPIDER's core product promise 'pay novelty not whole task' with repair boundaries, strong 0-token replay baseline, contamination and amortization economics, and verified byte-preserving substrate dependency. Either CONFIRMED (justifies repair architecture, unblocks residual-novelty amortization) or FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (exposes cheapest possible repair is not cheap, prevents premature promotion) materially changes claim state and next allocation for graph/runtime/product. Advances beyond 30-streak FRESHNESS saturation (r~0.002-0.046) which had diminishing marginal return; Director PIVOT rationale satisfied.
